title: Emulating Space Computing Networks with RHONE
problem: Space Computing Networks (SCNs) research requires high-fidelity modeling of satellite and constellation behavior (power, thermal, network, computation states), but real satellite experimentation is prohibitively expensive.
motivation: Affordable, high-fidelity emulation of satellite systems would enable broader research on Space Computing Networks without prohibitive operational costs.
method: RHONE uses a two-stage process. First, it builds models of satellite behavior—power consumption, heat, orbits, networking, and computation—by combining real satellite data with real chip code running in a simulator. Then it runs containerized applications (self-contained software packages) through these integrated models to simulate how entire satellite networks would function.
key_novelty: The core innovation is using real satellite data together with real chip code in a simulator to accurately model how satellites and constellations operate while remaining practical to use.
contributions: RHONE emulator enabling satellite and constellation-level fidelity for Space Computing Networks
Two-phase approach combining offline model building from real telemetry with online container-based emulation
Demonstrated accuracy: power and computation models with <5% error, thermal models within 1.3-2.5°C
Cost-effective evaluation platform for SCN research and application testing

metrics.accuracy: power/computation models <5% error, thermal models 1.3-2.5°C error
